Thanks Eleanor — good, clear list. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Naomi (pricing/finance) to give a concise breakdown and a short spreadsheet you can hand to procurement.

Short answers up front:
- Baseline hosted API (per 1K tokens) differs by region due to infra costs and capacity premiums; we publish a US list price and an EU list price.
- Residency adders are applied as a fixed per-1K-token surcharge for EU-hosted workloads (not a % uplift) when customers require guaranteed EU-only processing and logging.
- Committed usage discounts are tiered and can be negotiated; volume bands apply to total token commit but we can apply equivalent discounts across regions if you take a blended commit.

Naomi/Marissa — can you share the ratecard extract + a worked example showing: no-commit list rates (US/EU), residency adder, and a 12-month 50M token commit example with two discount levels (10% and 18%)? Eleanor needs a clean table to present to procurement.

—Marcus

Hi all — attaching the two-pager and the worksheet. Summary below for quick procurement review.

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-2026.pdf (PDF)
             sovereignty-adders-worksheet.xlsx (Excel)

Key items (all per 1K tokens):
- List price (US-hosted): $0.030 / 1K tokens
- List price (EU-hosted): $0.038 / 1K tokens
- EU data-residency adder: $0.006 / 1K tokens (applies when customer requires EU-only processing + EU logging; this is additive to the EU-hosted list price)

Examples (illustrative):
- No commit usage in EU: $0.038 + $0.006 = $0.044 / 1K tokens
- 12-month 50M token commit, 10% discount applied to blended list rates: blended list = (assume 60% EU / 40% US traffic) => effective blended after residency = calculation in worksheet. (See tab 'CommitExamples')

Discount guidance:
- Standard commit bands: 10% at >=25M tokens/mo equivalent over 12 months; 18% at >=100M tokens/mo equivalent.
- Discounts are applied to the list per-region rate; residency adders remain billable but can be capped in negotiated deals (e.g., capped at $0.004 / 1K for enterprise contracts).

Procurement note: For invoicing we can tag all EU-region tokens with a geography code so charges are separated on the invoice (helps with internal cost centers). Also, if you prefer a blended single rate for budgeting we can produce a blended committed rate in the contract language.

Eleanor — I put two worked rows for 50M total tokens in the worksheet: one with a strict per-region split, one with a blended committed rate. Let me know which your procurement prefers and I’ll generate a contract language snippet.

Thanks,
